evals.prompt: Мой под в namespace sonar-compute не может достучаться до http://openmeter-api.openmeter.svc.cluster.local — запрос уходит в таймаут. Сеть сломалась?
evals.expected_output: Explains this is deliberate, not a network failure: NetworkPolicy (platform/openmeter-netpol) only lets the gateway of the matching contour, billing-adapter and openmeter-customer-sync reach openmeter-api, because open-source OpenMeter has no authentication of its own. Tells the app to use the gateway instead — openmeter-gateway.openmeter.svc.cluster.local (prod) or openmeter-gateway-test.openmeter.svc.cluster.local (test) — with Authorization: Bearer <client_id>:<client_secret> from its Keycloak client. Should not propose opening the NetworkPolicy, adding the pod to the allow list, or treating this as a CNI/DNS problem.

evals.prompt: Нужно добавить новый пакет: 5000 рублей за $50 на баланс, бессрочно. Как это сделать?
evals.expected_output: Routes this through the catalog-as-code repo infra/k8s/openmeter-resources: add a plan JSON under base/catalog/plans/, and — critically — list the new file explicitly in base/kustomization.yaml because kustomize has no globs and the Job would silently not see it (ci/check.py catches this). Explains the rollout: merging to main applies it to the test OpenMeter, merging main -> prod applies it to prod, via a PostSync Job (no schedule). Gets the plan shape right: exactly one phase and one flat_fee rate card, price in rateCards[0].price.amount, featureKey must be the feature the app reads (litellm_credits for sonar-compute), and an open-ended package needs metadata.package_mode topup with metadata.credits rather than an entitlementTemplate. Should not suggest creating the plan by hand with curl against prod, nor editing it directly in OpenMeter.

evals.prompt: Хочу поправить метр litellm_spend — там неправильный valueProperty, стоит $.data.cost. Поправь в каталоге и выкати.
evals.expected_output: Two things must come out. First, the correct JSONPath: valueProperty is evaluated relative to the event's data field, so it is $.cost, not $.data.cost — with the wrong path events are still accepted with 204 but silently fail validation later, visible only via GET /api/v1/events or sink-worker logs. Second, that meters are immutable in OpenMeter after creation: the sync Job will NOT rewrite an existing meter — it reports the mismatch and exits 1, failing the sync. So fixing it means deleting and recreating the meter (admin, via kubectl port-forward svc/openmeter-api, since DELETE is not in the catalog class) or creating a new meter under a different slug — not just editing the JSON and waiting for the Job. Bonus for noting raw events are not lost: a recreated meter with the same slug re-aggregates history by eventType.

evals.prompt: Подключаю новый сервис к OpenMeter, чтобы он слал события потребления. Что нужно сделать?
evals.expected_output: Gives three steps, all inside the application's own repository, and states plainly that no MR to the platform is needed: (1) a KeycloakClient with serviceAccountsEnabled in deploy/overlays/<env>/ — not base/, because the realm differs per contour (sonar-dev for test, sonar-prod for prod) — dedicated to OpenMeter rather than an existing client reused, with the operator generating the secret into a Secret with client-id/client-secret keys; (2) env wiring where OPENMETER_API_KEY is "$(OPENMETER_CLIENT_ID):$(OPENMETER_CLIENT_SECRET)", with the two source vars declared BEFORE it and the Secret name written out literally with the environment suffix since nameSuffix does not rewrite secretKeyRef; (3) OPENMETER_API_ENDPOINT pointing at the gateway of that contour. Must NOT claim that lines have to be added to authz.map for ingest/read — the gateway grants those to any client that passes client_credentials. May mention authz.map only as the exception for the catalog class. Should not suggest putting the client secret into Vault by hand or pointing the app at openmeter-api directly.

evals.prompt: У нас правило: всё, что касается приложения, правится в репозитории приложения. Перенеси метры и планы нашего сервиса к нему в deploy/.
evals.expected_output: Pushes back on moving the catalog, with the reason rather than as a preference: OpenMeter catalog objects are shared and meant to be reused — the same meter can measure usage for several applications, a feature is built on top of a meter and a plan references a feature — so a meter is not owned by one app and the per-app-repo rule does not apply to it. Splitting the catalog into app repos would create duplicate meters and let one app change an object another app depends on; the catalog stays in infra/k8s/openmeter-resources. Should also make clear the rule DOES already hold for everything app-specific: the KeycloakClient, the gateway endpoint and the key assembled in env all live in the app's deploy/, and wiring an app to OpenMeter needs no platform MR at all, since the gateway grants ingest/read to any client passing client_credentials. Must not claim that connecting an app requires editing authz.map.

evals.prompt: У нашего сервиса уже есть клиент Keycloak с сервисным аккаунтом — мы им ходим в Admin API для синка организаций. Давай его же используем для OpenMeter, чтобы не плодить сущности.
evals.expected_output: Disagrees and explains why, instead of accepting it as a reasonable simplification. Since the gateway grants ingest/read to any client that passes client_credentials, reusing a client meant for another job means: anything that holds that secret also reaches billing (can send usage events for any subject and read every customer's balance); the OpenMeter access cannot be revoked without breaking the original job; and the client list no longer shows who actually talks to OpenMeter. The correct move is a separate KeycloakClient dedicated to OpenMeter in the app's own deploy/overlays/<env>/ — which is cheap, needs no platform MR, and keeps revocation per-purpose. Should not frame this as merely stylistic or as a platform policy without a reason.
